Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 8 (Term and Renewal) sits at our **preferred** position on all material terms:

- **Renewal length:** successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal, so nowhere near walk-away territory).

The three-year initial term in 8.1 is a negotiated commercial term rather than an auto-renewal defect, so it is not flagged under this rule.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: The structure of Section 21 is otherwise good: the cap is expressly mutual, indirect/consequential damages are mutually excluded (21.2), the Excluded Claims set in 21.3 covers confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP, and Customer's payment obligation is carved out of "damages". The failure is the cap quantum: it is measured by "Fees", which Section 1.5 defines as only the "Implementation Fee", i.e. the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (Section 1.6), and is further narrowed to the first Order Form. Recurring subscription and service charges are therefore excluded, making the cap illusory at roughly USD 12,000 — far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and inside walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees). Minimal redline changes only the cap base in 21.1 to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000; the existing carve-outs are left untouched.

proposal.summary: Replace the illusory cap base (Fees = USD 12,000 implementation fee under the first Order Form) with the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] As drafted the cap is measured by "Fees", which Section 1.5 defines as only the USD 12,000 one-time Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is effectively USD 12,000 and far below our floor of twelve months' charges. We have moved the cap to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000; the Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remain outside the cap as already drafted.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. input.rationale: The structure of Section 21 is otherwise good: the cap is expressly mutual, indirect/consequential damages are mutually excluded (21.2), the Excluded Claims set in 21.3 covers confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP, and Customer's payment obligation is carved out of "damages". The failure is the cap quantum: it is measured by "Fees", which Section 1.5 defines as only the "Implementation Fee", i.e. the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (Section 1.6), and is further narrowed to the first Order Form. Recurring subscription and service charges are therefore excluded, making the cap illusory at roughly USD 12,000 — far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and inside walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees). Minimal redline changes only the cap base in 21.1 to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000; the existing carve-outs are left untouched.

Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.rationale: Section 9.4, read with Section 29.4 (thirty days' notice), gives Customer a convenience termination right over the whole Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' written notice, with liability limited to accrued Fees and a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10 at p0045). There is no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the document, and no Vendor termination-for-convenience right — Vendor's termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1) and insolvency (9.2). This meets the preferred position in full; no redline needed.

paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 21.1 cap quantum.**

Section 21 is well-built in most respects: the cap is expressly mutual, 21.2 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully treats data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response as direct damages), 21.3 carries the full preferred carve-out set as "Excluded Claims", and Customer's payment obligation is excluded from "damages".

The defect is the cap base. The cap runs to "the **Fees** paid or payable by Customer under the **first Order Form**", and §1.5 defines "Fees" as only the "Implementation Fee" — a one-time USD 12,000 charge (§1.6). Recurring subscription and service charges fall outside the cap entirely, so the mutual cap is effectively ~USD 12,000: well below the fallback of 12 months' fees and into walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees).

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) makes the smallest possible change — only the cap base in 21.1 — to the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding 12 months and (b) USD 1,000,000. Carve-outs left untouched.

Noted but not flagged here: §7.7's 15%-per-week liquidated damages on late invoices is a separate commercial issue for the payment/remedies rule.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

paragraphs.text: 19. WARRANTIES

19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.

19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.

19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

paragraphs.text: 21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.
6. ACCEPTANCE

6.1 Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.

6.2 If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">Section 13 meets the preferred position on all material terms. The subscription grant in 13.1 expressly extends to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (no notice condition needed), and to Authorized Users; the paid-up grant in 13.2 is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid, including contractor support rights. Clause 13.3 permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24 — and § 24.1 allows assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent, with § 24.4 barring Vendor from terminating, repricing or suspending on our change of control. Revocation or suspension is limited to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity, so the licence is not revocable at will. The "Affiliate" definition (§ 1.1) is standard >50% control and is adequate. No redline required.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The ownership architecture in §§13–15 sits at our **preferred** position:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (§14.1):** Customer owns all Customer Data, Confidential Information, Customer-provided material and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right. Reinforced by §15.1 (no sale, no advertising use, no commingling, no model training without consent).
- **Deliverables (§14.2):** Customer owns each Deliverable on creation, with an express Vendor assignment, flow-down assignments from personnel, and further assurances.
- **Vendor IP (§14.3 + §13.2):** Vendor retains Vendor Technology only, and embedded Vendor Technology carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works — plus a pre-delivery identification duty and a bar on restrictive third-party material.
- **No joint ownership (§14.4):** excluded unless separately signed with exploitation rights; feedback is voluntary and Customer retains unrestricted rights in its own feedback.

Noted but not flagged: Deliverable ownership is conditioned on payment of Fees, and Vendor may process Customer material to "improve the Services for Customer." Both are standard and neither assigns Customer IP or data to Vendor.

paragraphs.text: 11. TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN

11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.

11.2 Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.

11.3 After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.
10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 18 (Insurance) meets the INSURANCE rule's **preferred** position on every material term:

| Requirement (preferred) | § 18.1 |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occurrence, 2M aggregate | ✅ Exact match |
| Professional E&O USD 2M | ✅ Exact match |
| Cyber/privacy USD 5M (Vendor processes Customer Data per §§ 15, 17) | ✅ Exact match |
| Workers' compensation as required by law | ✅ Plus employer's liability USD 1M (extra) |
| Certificates on request | ✅ § 18.2 |

The clause also carries the coverage through the term plus one year afterward, tracking our model language. Clause 18.2 adds several customer-favourable mechanics beyond the playbook ask — reputable insurers, primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities (preserving our indemnity and liability rights under §§ 20–21).

No further action needed on this rule.

Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position on every material term: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1); Deliverables materially conform to documentation and acceptance criteria for ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance, and Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term (19.2) — equal to or better than the preferred 90-day services / 12-month software benchmark; and 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and Applicable Law compliance warranties. The remedy in 19.4 is real: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item plus refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, and it is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties, is mutual, and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy; Section 21 likewise preserves caps without cutting back the warranty (and 21.4 survives failure of an exclusive remedy). Minor points noted only, not deviations: the refund is measured by "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable," and cure is owed "within a reasonable period" rather than a fixed cure window.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position on every material term: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1); Deliverables materially conform to documentation and acceptance criteria for ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance, and Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term (19.2) — equal to or better than the preferred 90-day services / 12-month software benchmark; and 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and Applicable Law compliance warranties. The remedy in 19.4 is real: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item plus refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, and it is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties, is mutual, and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy; Section 21 likewise preserves caps without cutting back the warranty (and 21.4 survives failure of an exclusive remedy). Minor points noted only, not deviations: the refund is measured by "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable," and cure is owed "within a reasonable period" rather than a fixed cure window.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

input.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with capped late-payment interest
input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any conceivable loss (and the remaining contract value). We have replaced it with customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the dispute-withholding right in Section 7.3.

ops.newText: If any undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month and the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar predetermined sum under this Agreement.

paragraphs.text: 2. AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.

2.2 Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

2.3 Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.
4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.
8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 13 (Access Rights and Licence) satisfies the LICENSE rule at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **Affiliates and contractors** — § 13.1 grants rights directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," with Authorized Users permitted to exercise them. This is better than the fallback (which would only require Affiliates on written notice), as no notice condition applies.
- **Paid-up licences** — § 13.2 is "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid," with broad use/modify/derivative-works rights and contractor support.
- **Not revocable at will** — § 13.3 limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity. Walk-away territory (revocable at Vendor's discretion) is not present.
- **Successor transfer** — § 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor under § 24, and § 24.1 allows Affiliate/M&A assignment without Vendor consent; § 24.4 further blocks Vendor from terminating, repricing or suspending on our change of control.
- **Definitions check** — "Affiliate" (§ 1.1) uses a standard >50%/management-control test, adequate for our group structure.

The only residual points are non-material and noted rather than flagged: the § 13.1 subscription grant runs for the subscription term (expected for hosted services), and Affiliate status lapses if the control relationship ends, which is customary.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 satisfies the preferred WARRANTY position on all material terms:

- **Performance standard (19.1):** professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus material conformity to documentation and specifications.
- **Duration (19.2):** 90 days from the later of delivery or acceptance for Deliverables, and Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term* — at or above the preferred 90-day services / 12-month software benchmark.
- **Additional warranties (19.3):** no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution, no source-code-tainting open source.
- **Remedy (19.4):** re-performance/repair/replacement at no charge, escalating to termination plus refund of Fees paid, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow it (19.5):** only implied warranties are disclaimed, mutually, with an express statement that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy. Section 21 caps liability but preserves Excluded Claims and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

Noted for information only (not deviations): refund is measured by "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable," and the cure obligation runs for a "reasonable period" rather than a fixed window.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us (Customer) of 15% of annual Fees for every week an invoice is late — an uncapped, compounding sum that would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value and is triggered by a mere ten-day payment delay. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (which contemplates only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties appear in the document; termination (Section 9.4) and force majeure (Section 27) are penalty-free, and no SLA credit construct runs against us. Redline deletes the liquidated-damages mechanic and substitutes customary simple interest at 1% per month on undisputed overdue amounts, aligned with the dispute-withholding protection in Section 7.3.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with capped late-payment interest
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any conceivable loss (and the remaining contract value). We have replaced it with customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the dispute-withholding right in Section 7.3.

ops.oldText: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: If any undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month and the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 11 ("Transition Assistance and Data Return") satisfies the preferred position on every material term:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Transition assistance up to 6 months at then-current rates | §11.1 — six months on Customer's request, at the rates in the expiring Order Form (**better than preferred**: locks legacy pricing) |
| Data return in standard machine-readable format within 30 days | §11.2 — thirty days, "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata" |
| Deletion + certification thereafter | §11.3 — secure deletion from active systems and backups, certified in writing by an authorized officer |

Additional customer-favourable protections worth noting: Vendor cannot withhold Customer Data over a fee dispute (§11.2), deletion is only triggered *after* we confirm successful return (§11.3), and any legally-required retained copy stays protected and purpose-limited. §10.1 independently preserves our Customer Data rights post-termination and expressly contemplates the transition period, so there is no hidden conditioning of data return on payment.

**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, Section 7.7 / p0032).**

- **Issue:** Section 7.7 requires *us* to pay Brightline "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of annual Fees **for each week** an invoice is unpaid, triggered after only ten days. Uncapped and compounding, it would quickly exceed the remaining contract value — walk-away territory, and well beyond the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' Fees).
- **Rest of document is clean:** Section 9.4 allows termination without cause with only accrued Fees owed; Section 27 termination is "without penalty"; there is no SLA credit or shortfall construct running against us.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** replaced the liquidated-damages mechanic with simple interest at the lesser of 1% per month or the legal maximum on *undisputed* invoices unpaid 30 days after due date, plus an express statement that we owe no liquidated damages or penalties — consistent with our Section 7.3 right to withhold genuinely disputed amounts.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: § 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment, confirms we pay only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, and states that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 12 (p0051), where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment, and by § 7.1 (p0026), which bars any unstated minimum-use charge. No take-or-pay, committed spend, non-reducible seat count, or volume cap on our usage appears anywhere; the only "shortfall" concept is the licence-audit true-up in § 22, which is a usage reconciliation rather than a purchase commitment. § 8.2 also gives us a 30 days' non-renewal right on each Order Form, so no commitment persists without an exit.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: § 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment, confirms we pay only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, and states that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 12 (p0051), where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment, and by § 7.1 (p0026), which bars any unstated minimum-use charge. No take-or-pay, committed spend, non-reducible seat count, or volume cap on our usage appears anywhere; the only "shortfall" concept is the licence-audit true-up in § 22, which is a usage reconciliation rather than a purchase commitment. § 8.2 also gives us a 30 days' non-renewal right on each Order Form, so no commitment persists without an exit.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The document satisfies the **preferred** position for MINCOMMIT — there is no minimum purchase commitment on us at all:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013)** is an affirmative disclaimer: "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 12 (p0051)** has Vendor acknowledge we made no exclusivity, MFC, or minimum-volume commitment.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026)** bars Vendor from imposing any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in the Order Form.
- **§ 8.2 (p0035)** gives us a 30-day non-renewal right per Order Form, with a reminder mechanic, so no commitment survives without an exit.

The only "shortfall" language (§ 22, p0095–p0096) is a licence-audit usage true-up, not a take-or-pay obligation, and it is expressly a true-up rather than a penalty — outside this rule's scope.

Two items noted but deliberately **not** flagged here, as they belong to other rules and flagging them under MINCOMMIT would double-count the commercial term:
- **§ 7.7 (p0032)** — 15% of annual Fees per week as "liquidated damages" for late payment is an aggressive late-payment remedy against us, but it is a payment-default charge, not a volume commitment.
- **§ 8.1** three-year MSA term is a framework term only; it carries no committed spend, so it is not multi-year take-or-pay.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side review)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — 19 rules assessed

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The Agreement is, on the whole, strongly aligned with our preferred positions: intellectual property, licence scope, indemnification, assignment and change of control, termination for convenience, transition assistance and data return, warranties, audit rights, renewal mechanics, governing law and insurance all meet the preferred position, and the Agreement affirmatively disclaims exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-volume, MFN and non-solicitation obligations on us (§§ 2.1, 12.3, 7.6). Vendor-side commitments in §§ 7.6 and 12.4 run in our favour and we leave them intact.

Two findings are deviations, and both sit in walk-away territory:

1. **Limitation of liability cap (§ 21) — critical.** The structure of § 21 is good (mutual cap, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, a broad Excluded Claims set covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP). The failure is the cap *base*: it is measured by "Fees," which § 1.5 defines as the "Implementation Fee" only — the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (§ 1.6) — and is further narrowed to the first Order Form. Recurring subscription and service charges are excluded, making the cap illusory at roughly USD 12,000, far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and inside walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees).
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — high.** Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on us of 15% of annual Fees for **every week** an invoice is late, triggered by a mere ten-day delay. The sum is uncapped and compounding and would rapidly exceed remaining contract value. This fails the fallback (which contemplates only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees) and is walk-away territory.

Both redlines are minimal and surgical: we change only the cap base in § 21.1 (leaving the carve-outs untouched) and replace the § 7.7 penalty with customary late-payment interest.

---

## Findings

|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## Walk-away items

We should treat the following as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** Because "Fees" is defined as the USD 12,000 implementation fee under the first Order Form, the effective cap is below six months' fees, which the playbook treats as walk-away. **Proposed redline:** replace the cap base with *the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000*. Fallback: twelve months' amounts paid or payable, without the USD 1,000,000 floor. The existing § 21.2 exclusions and § 21.3 Excluded Claims remain as drafted.
2. **§ 7.7 — uncapped, compounding liquidated damages against Customer.** 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment is a penalty in walk-away territory and exceeds the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees). **Proposed redline:** delete the liquidated-damages mechanic and substitute simple interest at 1% per month on undisputed overdue amounts, aligned with the dispute-withholding protection already in § 7.3.

---

## Next steps

1. Issue the two redlines above to Vendor as a single, short markup, with a covering note explaining that we are changing only the § 21.1 cap base and the § 7.7 late-payment remedy and are otherwise accepting §§ 7 and 21 as drafted.
2. Flag in the note that the § 1.5 definition of "Fees" is the root cause of the cap problem, so that any Vendor counter-proposal addresses the definition or the cap base rather than the carve-outs.
3. Confirm with the business owner the expected twelve-month run-rate spend, so we can validate that the USD 1,000,000 floor is the right ask on this deal.
4. Note for the file (no redline required): ownership of Deliverables under § 14.2 is conditioned on payment of Fees; § 19.4 measures refunds by "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable" and owes cure "within a reasonable period" rather than a fixed window. These are within market norms and we do not propose to raise them unless the counterparty reopens §§ 14 or 19.
5. Hold signature until both walk-away items are resolved; escalate internally if Vendor declines either.
